items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I had a book called Play in the Day. Burt Weedon’s Play in the Day.

ctx.x: Sight singing I was okay. Because I could sight read. I learned to sight read on a rainy afternoon when I was 11 years old. I had a book called Play in the Day. Burt Weedon’s Play in the Day. I mean you talk to anybody from that generation, they all learned out of Play in the Day. And in the back of the book was “When the Saints Go Marching in” and it’s in C and okay, that’s a C, that’s a C, I get it. It wasn’t rocket science.
Can I ask what your parents thought about your path?
